Definition: from G4314 and G2192; (figuratively) to hold the mind (3563 implied) towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to:--(give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard.
BiblicalUsage: Prosecho means to hold the mind toward something, to pay attention, to beware. Hebrews warns to give the more earnest heed to the things we have heard, lest we let them slip. Jesus says, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and, Beware of false prophets. Paul tells Timothy to give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe heed is the first duty of a hearer: the gospel slips away from the careless, leaven works quietly in the careless, and false prophets look harmless to the careless. I hold that attention is not a small thing; it is the difference between drifting and holding fast.
